claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the as-cast state.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance that limits high-temperature use.
Atomic layer deposition can provide a uniform 50–100 nm Al2O3 coating on the alloy.
A dense, well-adhered ALD alumina coating will significantly improve the alloy's oxygen resistance at high temperature.
The alumina coating can remain protective during exposure in air near 1000 °C for tens to hundreds of hours.
A conformal Al2O3 layer acts as a physical barrier to oxygen.
The coating prevents oxygen pickup by the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Oxygen pickup can cause embrittlement at grain boundaries and surfaces.
The high density and chemical inertness of ALD-deposited alumina impede oxygen diffusion into the refractory alloy.
Suppressing oxygen diffusion preserves the substrate's microstructural integrity.
Preserving microstructural integrity maintains the alloy's high-temperature yield strength and ductility.
Coated specimens will have lower oxygen uptake than untreated specimens after prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Coated specimens will form less oxide scale than untreated specimens.
Coated specimens will retain room-temperature tensile ductility similar to untreated cast material.
Coated specimens will retain elevated-temperature yield strength similar to untreated cast material.
Untreated HfNbTaTiZr undergoes significant oxidation-related degradation during high-temperature air exposure.
The coating is effective only while it remains adherent and intact during thermal cycling and mechanical loading.
Spallation or microcracking of the coating could compromise its oxygen-barrier effect.
